---
title: Migrating to 2.0
description: Update manifests and commands from the legacy PBS-only interface.
---

Version 2.0 makes a deliberate break from the implicit paths and embedded PBS
machinery used by earlier releases.

Inputs, outputs, and scheduler choices are now visible in the command or
manifest.

## Required changes

- Add the `run` subcommand. The pre-2.0 no-subcommand invocation is removed.
- Replace one-column sample lists and TopHat `accepted_hits.bam` discovery with
  an explicit `sample_id,bam_path` CSV manifest.
- Replace the standalone `merge-counts` executable with
  `htseq-count-cluster merge`.
- Update environments to Python 3.10 or newer and HTSeq 2.1 or newer.
- Expect count outputs named `<sample_id>.counts.tsv`; historical `.out` files
  are no longer discovered by the merge command.

## Scheduler behavior

After updating the command and manifest, confirm the scheduler behavior:

- The embedded PBS template and polling helper are removed.
- PBS commands are generated directly.
- Status checks run once instead of polling.
- Slurm uses one array job with optional `--max-concurrent` throttling.

Finish the migration with `--dry-run` at each cluster site. It:

- validates the inputs;
- prints the scheduler command; and
- does not consume allocation resources.

The result gives you a concrete command to compare with local scheduler policy
before the first 2.0 submission.
